newsitem.title: BERMUDA: RUGBY UNION - All Blacks mix it up at training.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION - All Blacks mix it up at training.

text.p: HAMILTON, June 25 - The All Blacks wasted no time in going for their first training run when they assembled in Hamilton yesterday afternoon, but there wasn't a rugby ball in sight.

They instead went for a 45-minute fartlek (a mixture of jogging and sprinting) run through Hamilton Gardens and along the Waikato River banks, as fitness trainer Martin Toomey continued to search for variety in a long and gruelling international season where boredom and over-training are the enemies.
The All Blacks learned from last year's tough international campaign the right balance of training is crucial to get through a modern test season.
"We try to mix it up, because it would be so easy to go over the top and then there's also the boredom thing," Toomey said.
"If you're trying to get people to do heaps of everything all the time you don't want them to go stale mentally," he said.
"We didn't train with the ball yesterday and that's quite a novelty for these guys."
Toomey said he had to be mindful of the tough travel and playing schedule coming up for the All Blacks, but he said they had learnt from last year's tough campaign.

"Those last couple of tests in South Africa at the end of last season: we felt players were losing fitness, so we thought let's avoid that this year and do a little bit more fitness work at the start of the season and taper off later."
They face a longer season this year in terms of time due to the end-of-season tour to Britain and Ireland, but it is less gruelling.
"We are three weeks into a 10-week block when we play eight tests, but then the players have the NPC as a recovery time before building again for that tour."
